To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified in 7 Tunisians with Rett syndrome a double mutation in a new hypothetical poly(A) site and a new variant in a hypothetical spicling enhancer in the 3’UTR of the gene MECP2.
we found a double mutation (p.R306C and 1461+98 insA) in a Tunisian patient with Rett syndrome, which is a new mutation in the MECP 2 gene.
we identified 2 novel mutations in the MEPC2 gene: p.R306 C and c.146 1+98ins A, in addition to a new variant c.1461+92 C>G.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new mutations and variants in the MECP 2 gene.
the first description of a double mutation of the MECP1 gene, and the presence of 2 new variants, which are not described in the literature, in Tunisian patients with Rett syndrome.
2 novel mutations: a double mutation in a patient and a new variant in another one, which could affect the polyadenylation process and the expression of the MECP 2 gene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the p.R306C mutation is a rare mutation in the MECP1 gene, and this is the first description in a Tunisian patient.
the p.T158M and p.R168 mutations are common mutations in Tunisian patients with Rett syndrome.
MECP2 is a complex gene and mutations are not only located in the coding region.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MECP2 mutations are the most frequent cause of classic Rett syndrome and the p.T158M mutation is the most common in the Tunisian population.
the p.R306C mutation is a novel mutation in the MECP 2 gene.
the most common mutations found in Tunisian Rett patients are the same as those found in other populations, but with different frequencies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the double mutation in 2 exons (p.R306C and 3′UTRs) of the MECP 2 gene could have an effect on the expression of MECP2 protein and may lead to the development of the disease.
MECP2 gene mutations are the most common cause of Rett syndrome.
